case_name: Rathinam @ Rathinan v State Of Tamil Nadu And Anr
facts: The facts have been taken from Criminal Appeal no. 905 of 2007.
Accused no.1, Rathinam is the son of the owner of Sundaram Textiles Waste Cotton Mill, Madam Sundarammal, situated at Erumal Thottam, Chinnavedampatti.
On 22nd December 1995 accused no.4 Sundaram, his wife Kalamani and one Sivakami attended the day shift which was over by 3.30 p.m.

Ravi thereafter left for the shop belonging to PW7 and as he came to the spinning section of the mill, he met the deceased who was to work the night shift and told her that he was going out to buy coconuts and cigarettes.

The dead body was also taken out of the well and was sent for the post-mortem examination which was duly conducted by Dr. Ramalingam PW 60 who found several injuries thereon including a ligature mark on both sides of the neck and a large number of other injuries including injuries on the genital organs.
PW 1 however made her independent inquiries and received information that the rape and murder had been committed only by Rathinam, A-1 and that Sundaram, A-4 was innocent.

The incident had happened in the late evening of 22nd December 1995 and it was for the prosecution to prove through the so called eye-witnesses PWs 4 and 5 that all 6 accused had been involved in the incident as that was the finding of the investigating agencies after further investigation.
court_reasoning: The Court observed that two reports had been filed by the investigating agencies which were at variance with each other in as much that the first final report attributed the rape and murder to Sundaram accused no.4 whereas the second final report after further investigation implicated Rathinam accused no.1 as the main accused and the others for the offence u/s. 201 of the Indian Penal Code.

The Court found that as per the statements of PW 1 her neighbour PW-2, and PW-3 the niece of the deceased that the latter had left for the mill with her mother at about 5.30 to 5.45 p.m. on the 22 December 1995 and thereafter PW 1 had returned home alone.

The Court then examined the evidence of PW 1 and PW 4 and observed that PW 1 had stated that she had left her daughter on the road near the mill and therefore there was thus no reason whatsoever to accept the presence of the deceased inside the premises at about 6.00 p.m. as her shift was to start at midnight.

The Court held that the explanation tendered by the prosecution about the presence of the deceased at 6.00 p.m. (that she was also doubling as a domestic servant in the house of Madam Sundarammal) could not be believed as there was absolutely no evidence to that effect.
holding: The trial court, accordingly, acquitted all the accused.
